scope: Research-only refinement of existing 7AG.4 effective compiler, selected linker-input, and runtime-image closure gates.

sources.name: GCC 15.1 spec files
sources.finding: File-level and spec-function includes use GCC's specs mechanism; include targets are not ordinary source-relative paths.

sources.name: GCC driver source
sources.finding: The current driver resolves %include and %:include through startfile_prefixes with multilib lookup enabled; %include_noerr allows missing targets.

sources.name: GCC developer options
sources.finding: -print-search-dirs and -print-sysroot report search context, not exact files read by a build invocation.

sources.name: GCC overall options
sources.finding: -### reports driver-generated child commands without executing them; -v prints commands during execution.

sources.name: Clang configuration files and toolchains
sources.finding: Default and nested @file configurations may inject options; -### previews commands, while actual commands and consumed bytes remain separate evidence.

sources.name: GNU ld scripts, file commands, and options
sources.finding: Links use a linker script; external scripts can include other scripts and load object/archive inputs. Link maps and verbose diagnostics provide selected-input evidence but do not prove runtime closure.

sources.name: MSVC include and link diagnostics
sources.finding: /showIncludes and /VERBOSE:LIB expose paths/selection; response files, default libraries, Windows SDK, and runtime identity still need explicit binding.

recommendations: Do not resolve GCC specs includes relative to the including file or via PATH; require exact resolved paths and content identities or retain unavailable/partial status.
Use a small synthetic include-policy matrix locally, then one native GNU/Linux audit with actual driver/linker diagnostics at the composed checkpoint.
Use MSVC /showIncludes, /VERBOSE:LIB, and /MAP only in a native Windows audit profile; hash selected inputs and preserve SDK/toolset/CRT identity.
Keep linked input closure and post-link runtime image closure as separate typed profiles.
Keep ordinary slices on focused fast tests; paired builds and platform audits remain scheduled checkpoints, not per-slice blockers.
